content:
- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Overestimates after sharp price spikes (e.g., 85+), often overshooting by 5–10% and failing to correct quickly.
- Shows persistent downward bias in the latter half of the forecast (last 10–15 days), suggesting mean reversion is not captured.
- Lags in response to recent price drops — forecasts remain high longer than actuals.
- Tends to overreact to short-term volatility, leading to overfitting to recent noise rather than underlying trend.
- Underestimates the magnitude of mean reversion after strong upward moves — fails to anticipate price pullback.
- Sensitive to initial conditions — forecasts are more inaccurate when history includes recent spikes or volatility.
